title: Korean Proverbs (속담 & 사자성어)
description: Classic Korean proverbs and traditional expressions with English meanings

items.translation: A piece of cake (Lit: Eating cold porridge).
Every little bit counts (Lit: Gathering dust makes a mountain).

items.target: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다.
items.translation: Nice words bring nice words back.
Pleasure comes after hardship.
Starting is half the battle.
Look before you leap (Lit: Tap even a stone bridge before crossing).

items.target: 낮말은 새가 듣고 밤말은 쥐가 듣는다.
items.translation: Birds hear day words, mice hear night words (Walls have ears).

items.target: 가는 말이 고와야 오는 말이 곱다.
items.translation: Nice words spoken lead to nice words returned (What goes around comes around).
Hollow puffed rice cake (All show and no substance).
Joy comes at the end of hardship (No pain, no gain).
Gathering dust creates a great mountain (Every little bit adds up).
A frog inside a well (A person of narrow vision).
Even monkeys fall from trees (Even experts make mistakes).
Even a sheet of paper is lighter when lifted together (Two heads are better than one).
Even Mount Geumgang is enjoyed after eating (Eating comes first).
Fixing the barn after losing the cow (Locking the stable after the horse bolts).
A tower built with devotion will not fall easily (Hard work never betrays).
A needle thief becomes a cow thief (Minor bad habits lead to major crimes).
Even on a familiar road, ask directions (Always double-check).
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
Giving a disease then offering medicine (Harming someone then pretending to help).
Eating rice cake lying down (A piece of cake).
Eating cooled porridge (Extremely easy).
Swimming while touching the ground (Effortless).
A rice cake in a painting (Unattainable desire).
Blood on a bird's foot (A drop in the ocean).
It is dark under the lamp (Overlooking what is right under one's nose).
Speak of the tiger and it appears (Speak of the devil).

items.target: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다.
items.translation: The frog forgets its tadpole days (Arrogance after success).
The thief's foot feels numb (A guilty conscience needs no accuser).

items.target: 뛰는 놈 위에 나는 놈 있다.
items.translation: Above a running person is a flying person (There is always someone better).
Habits formed at age three last until age eighty.

items.target: 발 없는 말이 천 리 간다.
items.translation: Footless words travel a thousand miles (Rumors spread fast).
Killing two birds with one stone (一石二鳥)
East question, West answer (An irrelevant answer) (東問西答)
A resolution lasting three days (Short-lived resolve) (作心三日)
Great vessels mature late (Great talents mature with time) (大器晚成)
Ten spoons make one bowl of rice (Many small contributions make a big difference) (十匙一飯)
If prepared, there is no worry (Preparation prevents disaster) (有備無患)
Thinking from the other person's shoes (Empathy) (易地思之)
Justice will eventually prevail (事必歸正)
Blue comes from indigo (The pupil surpasses the master) (青出於藍)
Sweetness comes after bitterness (苦盡甘來)
Fall seven times, stand up eight (Perseverance) (七顛八起)
Reap what you sow (自業自得)
Repaying a favor even beyond death (結草報恩)
Deep contemplation and careful thought (深思熟考)
One fish muddies the entire stream (一魚濁水)
Excess is as bad as deficiency (過猶不及)
Sharing joys and sorrows together (同苦同樂)
